Subject: EdgeWave private VPC — initial reference & questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is our rough topology and the internal network constraints that triggered a couple of follow-ups from our security team. We want to confirm the recommended demarcation between Redwood's control plane and our on-prem data plane, and understand any egress/telemetry behavior that will touch our perimeter.

Key asks from us:
- Can you confirm whether control plane traffic will originate from Redwood-managed IPs or a region-specific pool we should allow?
- How does KV cache / prefix caching behave if the data plane is in our colo — is any data mirrored to Redwood-hosted services?
- What's the suggested TLS/mTLS posture for the control->runtime channel (mutual certs, cert rotation cadence, can we integrate with our KMS)?
- Any special MTU/BGP recommendations for the attachment link, since we plan jumbo frames (9000 MTU) and BGP adjacency to our edge router.

I've attached the preliminary diagram (edgewave_vpc_reference_diagram_v1.pdf) and the security checklist our SOC wants filled. Looking for a concise technical response that we can hand off to our network ops team.

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: EdgeWave private VPC — initial reference & questions

Alex — thanks for the diagram and clear list. High level answers below; I also want to loop in Marissa and Jonas for operational runbook and topology details.

Summary answers (short):
- Control plane egress: Redwood control plane initiates from region-addressable pools we manage. We can provide a signed IP range list for your firewall allowlist; for Dedicated/private customers you can enable static egress IPs or set up a VPN tunnel to eliminate dynamic ranges.
- KV cache: runtime KV/prefix cache is local to the on-prem data plane when you run Redwood Private in your colo. No customer content is mirrored back to Redwood-hosted services by default. Telemetry (metrics/traces) can be routed to your telemetry collector only.
- TLS/mTLS: we recommend mTLS with mutual certs for control->runtime. We support customer-managed CAs and integration with external KMS (AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault / HSM). Cert rotation cadence: default 90 days, configurable to match your SOC policy.
- MTU/BGP: 9000 MTU is fine; ensure path MTU across any intermediate link is consistent. For BGP, prefer eBGP with explicit next-hop advertisement from your edge router; advertise /29 for the attachment and use BFD for quicker failure detection.

Action items for next steps:
1) Marissa — can you prepare a one-pager with the static IP ranges and optional VPN configuration we can give EdgeWave operations?
2) Jonas — please draft an ops-runbook snippet describing cert bootstrapping, rotation, and KMS integration steps.
3) Alex — if you can share the completed egress checklist we will annotate and return it.

I'll follow up internally with a more detailed topology note (control plane flows, telemetry endpoints, and NAT/eProxy expectations).

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Alex's diagram and their SOC's checklist (attached previously). I've sketched an initial recommendation below; please review and add concrete snippets we can hand back to them. We want to be prescriptive but not prescriptive enough to force a specific topology.

Quick recommended demarcation (technical):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed):
  * Runs in our region control cluster; control RPCs to on-prem runtime over TLS+mutual auth.
  * Exposes management endpoints on port 8443 (TLS) and metrics on 9100 (optional).
  * Egress can be pinned to static IPs via a customer-dedicated egress nat gateway or tunneled over IPsec.
- Data plane (EdgeWave on-prem):
  * Runs inside customer-provided tenant network; runtime nodes own KV caches and model artifacts are pulled on-demand from the customer-accessible registry or cached locally.
  * No persistent customer PII or prompts are forwarded to Redwood-hosted services; logs and telemetry are configurable to stay in-customer.

Networking specifics to include in our reply:
- BGP: prefer single-hop eBGP with MD5 and BFD, advertise a /29 for the attachment. Provide sample neighbor configs for Cisco/Juniper.
- MTU: set 9000 on internal interfaces; ensure GRE/VXLAN encapsulation overhead accounted for (reduce inner MTU by 50 bytes if using VXLAN).
- NAT/eProxy: if the customer requires outbound NAT, document expected source ports and connection lifetime for long-lived control channels (we use keepalive; propose 15s TCP keepalive).
- mTLS details: 2-way TLS with CN format redwood-runtime-<tenant>-<nodeid>; rotation via SCEP/Simple PKI or Vault; provide sample cert CN policy.
- Observability: metrics exported via Prometheus exporter; traces forwarded to OTLP endpoint under customer's control.

Deliverables to produce (owners):
- Marissa: static IP list + VPN config doc (output: edgewave-redwood-ips-v1.pdf)
- Jonas: cert bootstrapping and rotation runbook (output: controlplane-cert-runbook.md)
- Kimberly: a short note on telemetry retention and how to configure OTLP endpoint and S3 ingestion (output: telemetry-ops-notes.md)

Please add any further risks or missing items inline. I want to turn this into a 1-page annotated topology and a short checklist to feed back to their SOC by EOD.

Best,
Vivek

Vivek / team — really helpful, thanks. Quick clarifications from Security before we hand to NetOps: 

- Static IPs and VPN: we prefer static egress NATs for allowlisting. Can you provide RFC 1918-friendly NAT behavior and expected PTRs?
- KV cache: good to hear the data plane keeps cache local. Can you confirm whether model weights or artifacts are pulled via HTTP(S) from Redwood or from a customer-hosted registry? We want the ability to host artifacts internally.
- Cert rotation: 90 days default OK; can you also provide an offline cert bootstrap example for airgapped customer nodes?

Next steps: we'll feed this to our NetOps and SOC. I've uploaded the annotated diagram with a couple of marginal notes and an egress checklist we started — please annotate and return (linked). If you can give the static-IP list and a one-page cert bootstrap snippet by EOD we'd be in great shape.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EdgeWavePrivateVPC (diagram + checklist uploaded)

Thanks,
Alex
